comments:

Thank you for reporting this.

> Maybe it would help not to add the device when all the newly discovered entities already exist, add newly discovered entities to the existing device or delete stale devices that do not have any entities anymore.

The ssdp-config-flow should be aborted when the unique id of the entry (`{udn}::{st}`) is already configured (or ignored.) Can you enable additional logging to get some more information? You can do this by adding this to you `configuration.yaml`:
```
logger:
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.upnp: debug
    async_upnp_client: debug
```

You have already mailed it I see, thank you!

I have analyzed the log file and am uncertain what is going on. It seems a new `config_entry` can be created while there already is a `config_entry` with the same `unique_id`. Normally, the config flow mechanism check if there isn't already a `config_entry` with the same `unique_id`, if so, the flow is aborted.

In this case, the `tg61` device is discovered via SSDP and added while there already are multiple `config_entries` for it. After discovery, it seems you have added it. Is that correct? (Which is fine, you should have never seen the newly discovered device any how...)

You don't seem to have the `upnp` component enabled in your `configuration.yaml`. So this cannot be the cause.

What happens when you remove all the upnp integrations and re-add them? After removing the integrations, please also check your `.homeassitant/.storage/core.config_entries` file and clean those as well (search for `"domain": "upnp"`), and restart home assistant.

Also, are you able to edit the integration sources/add more logging statements?

I made some more experiments including you suggestions.

I noticed two strange things: 

1. when I select one of the detected devices to be configured, it shows a different device in the end. In the screenshot I clicked on the tg61 configure button
![Screenshot_20200926_120959](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32200649/94339248-b1e88780-fff8-11ea-877e-9cfc9d181008.png)
2. in the `core.config_entries` file the device is sometimes detected as `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:WLANAccessPointDevice` (which sounds correct for the TG61 device) an sometimes as `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice`. In the example above the wrong device (Fritz!Box) got the `WLANAccessPointDevice`

I think I can add logging.
`urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:WLANAccessPointDevice` is something worth looking into, only the `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice` should be used. Let me check the logging you sent.

I think that is the problem, well spotted. When the `config_entry` is created, it is given the `unique_id` by concatenating `UDN::ST` (UDN being Unique Device Name, for example `uuid:upnp-InternetGatewayDevice-1_0-889ffacb9043`, ST being Search Target, for example `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1`.) See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e08934ee4c81e5346241357828ddba3cedd1c3ed/homeassistant/components/upnp/config_flow.py#L149-L154

Once the `config_entry` is created, it is initialized. Upon initialization, the `unique_id` of the `config_entry` is checked and corrected if needed. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e08934ee4c81e5346241357828ddba3cedd1c3ed/homeassistant/components/upnp/__init__.py#L122-L127

If I remember correctly, this is mostly for historical reasons and am not sure if this still needed or not. I think it was there for the case when the integration was activated from `configuration.yaml`.

In this case it actually hurts. During the initialisation process the `unique_id` of the device (which should be the same as the `unique_id` of the `config_entry`) is determined differently. The `deviceType` from the XML-device-description of the device is taken. In your case this is not the expected `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1`, but `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:WLANAccessPointDevice` as you pointed out. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e08934ee4c81e5346241357828ddba3cedd1c3ed/homeassistant/components/upnp/device.py#L105-L108

In the log files you've sent me before, look for the line `2020-09-18 17:47:52 DEBUG (MainThread) [async_upnp_client.traffic] Got response:`. Below that is the XML-device-description with the incorrect(?) `deviceType`.


I'll check if the checking/correcting the `unique_id` is still required during the initialization. If not, removing this will probably fix your problem. You can already test this yourself by finding the removing these lines https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e08934ee4c81e5346241357828ddba3cedd1c3ed/homeassistant/components/upnp/__init__.py#L122-L127 If you have any results, please post them here.

Still, to be fair, I think your device does not fully announce itself correctly or has a broken device-description. Nevertheless, if it can be circumvented, or in this case it might even be a problem in the integration, lets try to fix it.
Your suggested change seems to do the trick. The devices are detected once and only once and without mix up now.
Great, thank you for testing! The PR is currently being reviewed. Hopefully it'll be included in the next version.

review_comments: What if there's a config entry that was previously imported and lacks the correct unique_id? It will now be loaded and keep lacking a unique id, right?

Yes, there is a small window between `async_step_import()` and this, `async_setup_entry()`, in the pre-PR version. I think the window is very small and doubt there are users who have this.

In the new version the `unique_id` is always set via the config flows.
`async_step_user()`: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f87c9247750af65512a58546b406f72e4c522d4d/homeassistant/components/upnp/config_flow.py#L60
`async_step_import()`: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f87c9247750af65512a58546b406f72e4c522d4d/homeassistant/components/upnp/config_flow.py#L138
`async_step_ssdp()`: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f87c9247750af65512a58546b406f72e4c522d4d/homeassistant/components/upnp/config_flow.py#L163

As far as I know there is no path to `async_setup_entry()` without either going through either an existing entry, where it is already set, or the config flows, where it is always set now.

If I'm wrong please let me know. Then I'll change it to something like:
```
    if not config_entry.unique_id:
        hass.config_entries.async_update_entry(
            entry=config_entry,
            unique_id=device.unique_id,
        )
```

Before this PR we didn't set unique_id in the import step. So a config entry could have been created via import and then the config yaml removed. Then the config entry would upon loading not have the correct unique_id, from what I can see.

Possible, but the config_entry is directly activated as far as I know. So the window would be fairly small.

Nevertheless, I've added my suggested snippet.
I think this covers your case. Thank you for the review.
Ok, I think you're correct that the old imported entry would receive the unique id here directly after creation.
Please add a test for this case.
